text: David knew what sheep were like.
They needed a shepherd.
God was his Shepherd.
A good shepherd did not merely own sheep.
He stayed with them.
He led them to grass when they were hungry.
To quiet water when they needed rest.
That was enough for the day.
The sheep did not have to know every path.
They had to know the shepherd's voice.
The Shepherd was good, and the Shepherd was near.
The path did not stay on green hills.
Sometimes it went down into shadow.
But God was closer.
A shepherd did not abandon the sheep when the path turned dark.
That was when his presence mattered most.
The valley was not a sign that the shepherd had failed.
It was part of the journey he would lead them through.
Both were mercy.
The valley had shadows, but shadows were not the final word.
David kept walking because the Shepherd was there.
He was going through.
Then the picture changed.
David was no longer only a sheep in the field.
The table was.
A table means welcome.
It means someone has made room for you.
It means help is not thrown at you from a distance.
Placed before you with care.
The enemies could not cancel the Shepherd's care.
The table was a quiet kind of victory.
Not loud.
That was the sound of grace.
Psalm 23 ends with home.
David looked ahead and saw goodness and mercy following him all the days of his life.
The Shepherd would not stop being faithful.
Goodness and mercy did not merely visit David.
They followed him.
That is a strong picture, like God's kindness staying close behind him through every road, every field, every valley, and every battle.
David's life had not been easy.
It was in God's steady care.
David wanted to dwell in the house of God forever.
That was the end of the song, and it was the deepest comfort.
Forever.
